title: Open WebUI alternative for Ollama, with no server to run · {name}
description: {name} is a folder of static files. Point it at Ollama or LM Studio and it answers from your machine, with MCP built in and nothing to deploy but a web page.
h1: An Open WebUI alternative for Ollama, with no server to run
lede: {name} is a folder of static files. Point it at Ollama or LM Studio and it answers from your machine, with MCP connections, files in and out, and nothing to deploy but a web page.
facts: Ollama, LM Studio, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
setting.title: One setting first
setting.text: Ollama answers a web page only once it allows that page’s address. In LM Studio, turn on CORS. {name} shows the same line when you add the server.
fair.title: Open WebUI, fairly
fair.body: Open WebUI is the best-known self-hosted chat for Ollama: a Python app you run with Docker or pip, with user accounts and roles, documents, tools and an admin console, built to run entirely offline. It is free to self-host, and its licence keeps its branding on any deployment with more than 50 users in 30 days, unless you have written permission or an enterprise licence.
table.rows: A folder of static files on any web server, or {domain} itself.
A Python app and its database, SQLite by default; Docker is the recommended way.
No accounts to manage: each browser is its own. At work, a policy file sets brains and rules for everyone.
User accounts, roles and groups, in an admin console.
Ollama, LM Studio, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, provider keys, plans, and one that runs in the browser.
Built in, signed in from the browser; a gateway for servers a browser can’t reach.
Natively since v0.6.31, Streamable HTTP only; other servers through its mcpo proxy.
Word, Excel, PowerPoint, charts and pages that work, with numbers worked out by code in a sandbox.
Answers with web sources, Python it runs in the browser or a terminal, and pictures it makes.
The Open WebUI License: BSD-3 terms, plus a clause keeping its branding beyond 50 users in 30 days.
Pull a new image or package; the database migrates as it starts.
better.title: Where Open WebUI does better
better.items: One shared server: everyone’s chats, documents and models in one place, with roles.
An admin console for users, models and usage.
Documents shared across a team, searched on the server.
A large ecosystem of functions, tools and pipelines.
both.title: Use both
both.cards: Keep Open WebUI for the team’s shared space. Give people {name} for their own files, pointed at the same models.
A static folder beside it, served by the Caddy or nginx you already run.
The servers you connected there connect to {name} too, when they answer a browser.
catch.items: Ollama must allow {name}’s address, or LM Studio have CORS on.
No shared space: each person’s work lives in their own browser. Back it up, or sync it on a computer.
No admin console. At work, a policy file sets brains, rules and connections.
MCP servers must answer a browser, or go through a gateway you run.
faq.items: No. It is static files; the browser does the rest. Ollama, or whatever AI you point it at, answers.
